Doing the weekly shopping today I crossed a line I never even imagined could happen. I live in a town that used to be relatively fit but has gone to the fats a little more each year. It used to be very unusual to see a person who was 300 pounds - now I see them every day and 400+ pounders in their goddamned grocery store scooters clogging the aisles is common. Yet nothing prepared everyone at the supermarket for what we saw today.

In the produce section, I saw several of the produce clerks standing around something that looked like a long, thin piece of raw, greyish fish. I didn't pay much attention. It didn't register really, I guess I just thought someone had tracked some fish into the produce section and they were annoyed. I pick up everything I need and proceed to the dairy section. I get my milk and go to the bread aisle and there I see it. And after a second I smell it, too.

I honestly cannot believe this. I've been a member here since before Reddit banned the community and we came to Voat and a couple of years ago I would have read this and thought, "Yeah, whatever, that totally happened." We are quickly reaching the Rubicon, folks. What I am about to describe may one day be so common no one reacts.

At the end of the aisle was a severely obese man. He probably weighed around 400-500 pounds, was wearing shorts even though it was a cool day, and was riding in a scooter. He was looking on the back of a bag of bread, reading the nutritional label. At first I didn't really know what I was seeing until I got close enough to smell him. You know how people with uncontrolled diabetes have sores and discolored legs? This man had that happening, and it was the worst I've ever seen. I tried to find a picture online to demonstrate it and couldn't find one bad enough. His legs looked like a roll of deli bologna that was left to rot and then grated with a cheese grater. Little slivers of grey, dead skin, just hanging around pockets of scabby, reddish and greenish meat/skin/scabs.

It all hit me at once. The grey shredded-looking skin, the smell... He was more or less rotting, and had received some sort of debridement treatment. I think he had done some wound debridement because one leg around where his calf would be was wrapped in white bandage gauze, with yellowy-greenish fluid seeping into it. The reek coming off this man was nothing I have ever experienced before. I had to turn around and leave the aisle. I didn't even think to photograph it. It was an immediate reaction, I had to get away from him.

As I was fleeing to a part of the store without his odor, the worst of the horror hit me. That long strip in the produce department came from him. He lost a strip of his skin and did nothing about, but that also assumes he could even feel it. I wonder if he has any sensation in his legs at all. Those poor produce workers likely didn't want to deal with it or maybe didn't even how to deal with it. Is it a biohazard? Surely it is. Is dealing with zombie skin falling off fat people covered in the employee manual?

People were genuinely aghast at what we were seeing. An older (thin, of course) woman in nurse's scrubs looked at me and we just stared at each other for a moment. She shook her head in disbelief. I had to leave. I hate it when people pick up stuff in stores and don't put the items back. I worked in retail for many years and am always aware of what I do in stores. But I had no choice. I had to leave a cart filled with perishables behind so I could get some fresh air before I vomited. I didn't puke but I also didn't go back inside. I just left.

He said police often just get rid of everything they were wearing when they come across a decomposing body because the smell never goes away. I immediately showered and put my clothes in the wash and I still swear I get little whiffs of it. Thank god I didn't check out and bring home food from that store.

The worst part of this is that he may have been used to how he smells but he knows he is rotting. He knows he has shreds of dead skin hanging from his legs. Yet he blithely wandered around in public.
